title: Emergencies - what to do
content: If someone is in immediate danger (trouble breathing, chest pain, heavy bleeding that will not stop, unconsciousness, seizure, signs of a stroke, severe allergic reaction, poisoning or overdose), call the free national ambulance service 1990 (Suwa Seriya) straight away or go to the nearest hospital emergency department. Police emergency: 119. National mental health helpline (NIMH): 1926. University Medical Center emergency contact: <<FILL IN: Medical Center emergency phone number>>. Serious emergencies need hospital emergency care.

content: The University Medical Center provides primary healthcare for university students: consultations with a doctor and a pharmacy that dispenses prescribed medicines. title: Registering as a patient
content: New students register once using the 'Register here' link on the login page. You enter first name, last name, NIC number, address, AR number and a password of at least 8 characters. Height, weight and special medical conditions (for example allergies, asthma or diabetes) are optional but helpful, because the doctor can see them. Your AR number becomes your username. Students who cannot register online can be registered at the counter by the Counter Officer.

title: Logging in
content: Log in with your AR number as the username and the password you chose when registering. Forgotten password: <<FILL IN: how a forgotten password is handled>>.

title: Tokens - how the queue works
content: A token is your place in the queue to see a doctor. Students can issue their own token after logging in: open the dashboard and press 'Get today's token'. The Counter Officer can also issue one after checking your Campus ID and AR number. Token numbers start again from 1 every day, and a token only works on the day it was issued. You can hold only one active token at a time (status Pending or In-Consultation); once your consultation is Completed you can get a new one. Your dashboard shows your token number, its status and how many patients are ahead of you.

title: At the counter - what to bring
content: At the counter, bring your Campus ID and know your AR number. The Counter Officer checks them against your record, can register you manually if you have no record yet, and can issue today's token for you.

title: What happens during a visit
content: 1) Get a token (online from your dashboard, or at the counter). 2) Wait for your turn; your dashboard shows how many patients are ahead. 3) When your token is called the status changes to In-Consultation and you see the doctor. 4) The doctor records the diagnosis and prescribes medicines that are in stock; the prescription is sent digitally to the pharmacy. 5) The pharmacy packs the medicines and you collect them by showing your token number. There are no appointments; the service works through daily tokens.

title: Doctor availability
content: Two doctors (Doctor 1 and Doctor 2) work at the Medical Center. The 'Doctor availability' panel on the student dashboard shows whether each doctor is currently available; the doctors update their own availability. If neither is available, ask at the counter.

title: Pharmacy and collecting medicines
content: After the doctor saves your prescription it appears in the pharmacy queue by token number. Your dashboard first shows 'being prepared at the pharmacy' and later 'dispensed'. Show your token number to the pharmacist to collect your medicines. Doctors can only prescribe medicines that are currently in stock. If you think something is missing from your pack, ask the pharmacist.

title: Your medical history
content: Use 'My Medical History' on your dashboard to see your past visits: date, time, diagnosis, prescribed medicines and whether they were dispensed. Only you can see your own history; the doctor can view it during your consultation.

title: Privacy and this assistant
content: This AI assistant cannot see your records, tokens or prescriptions and cannot access your account. Please do not share your NIC number, password or detailed personal medical information in the chat. For anything about your own account, use your dashboard or ask at the counter.

title: Medicines and prescriptions
content: Only the Medical Center doctors prescribe medicines. The assistant cannot recommend prescription medicines or doses, or diagnose a condition. For medicines the doctor has prescribed, follow the label and the pharmacist's instructions, and never share your medicines with others.

title: First aid: minor burns
content: For a minor burn or scald: cool the area under cool (not ice-cold) running water for at least 10 to 20 minutes, remove rings or tight items near the area before it swells, then cover loosely with a clean non-fluffy dressing or cling film. Do not burst blisters and do not apply butter, toothpaste or ice. See a doctor urgently for large burns, burns on the face, hands, genitals or joints, deep or white/charred skin, chemical or electrical burns, and any burn in a young child.

title: First aid: minor cuts and grazes
content: For a minor cut: wash your hands, press firmly on the wound with a clean cloth for several minutes to stop the bleeding, rinse gently with clean running water, then cover with a clean dressing. See a doctor if bleeding does not stop after 10 to 15 minutes of firm pressure, the wound is deep or gaping, dirty, caused by an animal bite or a rusty object, or your tetanus vaccination may not be up to date.

title: First aid: nosebleed
content: For a nosebleed: sit up and lean slightly forward (not back), pinch the soft part of the nose firmly for 10 to 15 minutes without letting go, and breathe through your mouth. Seek medical help if it lasts more than 20 minutes, follows a head injury, or happens often.

title: First aid: sprains and strains
content: For a sprain or strain: rest the area, apply a cold pack wrapped in a cloth for 15 to 20 minutes several times a day, use a firm (not tight) bandage and keep the limb raised. See a doctor if you cannot put weight on it, the pain is severe, the joint looks deformed, or you feel numbness or tingling.

title: Fever, colds and flu-like illness
content: For a mild fever or cold: rest, drink plenty of fluids and eat light meals. See a doctor if the fever lasts more than 2 to 3 days or is very high, or if it comes with a severe headache, stiff neck, rash, trouble breathing, confusion, repeated vomiting or signs of dehydration. Ask the doctor or pharmacist before taking any medicine and follow the label.
